subject: health
unitTitle: How My Body Works and Stays Well
title: Explicit model: germs and how illness spreads
essentialQuestion: How do my body systems and my daily habits work together to keep me well?
materials: a simple body-systems diagram or model
paper or a digital tool for a prevention routine
keyPoints: Bacteria and viruses are different: antibiotics work on bacteria and do nothing to viruses.
Germs spread by droplets from coughs and sneezes, by direct contact, by contaminated surfaces, and through food and water.
Someone can pass on an illness before they feel ill themselves.
Breaking one link in the chain — washing, covering, staying home, cleaning surfaces — stops the spread.
privacySafeScenario: One person in a class has a stomach bug on Monday and six do by Friday. Trace the likely routes and name the two changes that would help most.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about germs and how illness spreads to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about germs and how illness spreads in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about germs and how illness spreads.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Diagrams may be replaced with text descriptions, tactile models, or spoken explanation. Any routine step a learner cannot perform independently is planned as an adult-supported step, which counts fully.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about germs and how illness spreads under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, find out where the household keeps its first-aid supplies and the doctor or clinic contact details. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
